grades.quote: if is a normal fence and it has `.pr` set, all program-order-previous load instructions are finished;
grades.reason: Operational-model commit condition for a fence. It shows the predecessor bits (.pr/.pw) pick which earlier loads or stores must be finished. It says nothing about the successor bits and doesn't explain what the fields select in general.

grades.quote: The address space is divided by the execution environment into memory and I/O domains, and the FENCE instruction provides options to order accesses to one or both of these two address domains.
grades.reason: Covers aq/rl ordering of atomics. It only says that FENCE has options to order accesses to the memory and I/O domains. It does not describe the predecessor and successor fields.

grades.quote: The predecessor set includes loads (resp.stores) if and only if PR (resp.PW) is set. Similarly, the successor set includes loads (resp.stores) if and only if SR (resp.SW) is set.
grades.reason: Directly explains that the predecessor set is the earlier accesses and the successor set is the later accesses. PR/PW select loads/stores in the predecessor set, and SR/SW select them in the successor set.

grades.quote: Note that the FENCE instruction distinguishes between main memory operations and I/O operations in its predecessor and successor sets. To enforce ordering between I/O operations and main memory operations, code must use a FENCE with PI, PO, SI, and/or SO, plus PR, PW, SR, and/or SW.
grades.reason: Explains that the predecessor and successor sets distinguish main-memory operations from I/O operations. PI/PO/SI/SO select I/O and PR/PW/SR/SW select memory. It covers only the I/O side and is cut off before its example.
